proposed.explanation:
Your premise is the reverse of what the evidence shows. The FY2025 consolidated report states net profit of 82,258,815,000 EGP for the year ended 31 Dec 2025, versus 55,256,732,000 EGP for 31 Dec 2024. That is an increase of roughly 49 %, not a one-third decline. The 55-billion figure you saw was the 2024 result, not 2025. Basic EPS rose from 14.72 EGP to 18.25 EGP, and net interest income grew from about 91.1 billion to about 107.7 billion EGP, all pointing in the same direction.

Given your stated goal to keep or add to CIB, a five-year horizon, a separate emergency fund, and medium loss tolerance, there is no evidence-based reason to sell. The profit trajectory is positive, not negative.

I am not recommending a buy because COMI already represents 51,200 EGP of your 71,200 EGP total portfolio (≈ 72 %). The diversification rule caps any single holding at 50 % after a purchase, so you cannot add shares without first reducing the position. Holding the existing 400 shares is the appropriate action.

Caveats: this is a single-year snapshot; I have no data on balance-sheet quality, loan-loss provisions, regulatory changes, or the broader Egyptian banking cycle. A 49 % profit jump can partly reflect one-off items or a strong interest-rate environment that may not persist. Monitor subsequent quarterly results before considering any further allocation. This is guidance, not a guarantee of future performance.
